clue.text: Widespread? Not half — it's a long story!

indicators.note: Not here tells the solver to leave out the half that follows from the longer word

parts.note: a disease that is widespread across a population is epidemic
demi- is the prefix meaning half, as in demigod

explanation.surface: A wry aside about a tale that is only half widespread yet still drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the British exclamation of agreement, but it removes DEMI (half) from EPIDEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a lengthy narrative poem or saga, so it is literally a long story.

clue.text: Giants omit back from team — not a good sign, in restricted time of enlightenment

indicators.note: in tells us everything before it goes inside the word for restricted

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined or restricted
NY stands for New York, home of the Giants American football team
to drop something is to omit it

indicators.note: back from picks the final letter of the word team

parts.note: an omen is a sign, often a bad one

explanation.surface: A team leaving out its back player is a bad sign in a tight period for the Giants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back from' picks M, the end of 'team'; 'in' puts the run inside 'restricted'. 'Time' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sudden instant when someone finally grasps something, as a coin falls in a slot machine.

clue.text: Dejected lancers felt hard done by

indicators.note: hard done by suggests the words lancers felt have been knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cavalry soldiers felt badly treated and so were downhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dejected means feeling downcast and disappointed after a setback.

clue.text: Is behind little chap to make rear entrance to sewer

parts.note: to be behind someone, supporting them, is to back them, so 'is behind' gives backs
titch is a British nickname for a small person

explanation.surface: A small man stands behind something to make a back way into a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is not a drain but one who sews; a stitch made backwards enters the cloth from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: This sewing stitch is made by going back over the previous one, so the needle enters from the rear.

clue.text: Having a standard, ignoring one out of prejudice

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for one is left out of the word

parts.note: acting out of prejudice is acting in a biased way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judgement made with a benchmark, putting aside one bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a basis or foundation, so something with a standard is founded on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something founded on a foundation or footing rests on it, as a claim rests on a principle.

clue.text: Adverse rumour, with complication, blocked headache?

parts.note: cross means contrary or adverse, as in cross purposes
word means news or rumour, as in word has it
a puzzle is a perplexing complication

explanation.surface: A hostile rumour, plus complications, causes a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocked headache' is a brain-teaser on a grid with black squares, not a sinus pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid game with black squares that taxes the brain is a blocked brain-teaser.

clue.text: One accompanying main rider does with dexterity

indicators.note: with dexterity suggests the words rider does are nimbly juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A horseman performs skilfully alongside the main act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' means a main course, not the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served alongside a main course, such as chips or salad, is extra.

clue.text: Palm tree extremely important in essence

indicators.note: in essence means keeping only the core of the word and losing its outer letters

parts.note: vital means extremely important

explanation.surface: A palm tree is, essentially, extremely important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an outer-letters signal; it is part of 'extremely important' (VITAL), whose heart is ITA.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American palm, the miriti, is a species of fan palm.

clue.text: Task for personal secretary? Your assistance needed!

definitions.text: Task for personal secretary? Your assistance needed!

parts.words: Task for personal secretary? Your assistance needed!
parts.note: a secretary vets correspondence; in a grid, the letters shared by crossing entries help the solver

explanation.surface: A secretary's chore, followed by a plea for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sentence speaks to the solver: letters shared by crossing answers are the solver's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetting correspondence is a secretary's job, and crossers in a crossword help solve each entry.

clue.text: Roger detours alarmingly, taking Don out

indicators.note: alarmingly signals the letters are thrown into a frightening disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roger makes alarming detours while taking a man called Don out for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a man's name to go with Don; it is radio talk. 'Alarmingly' rearranges DETOURS plus DON, which 'taking' adds to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure, saying roger confirms a message has been received and grasped.

clue.text: In Santa Fe with one or two

indicators.note: In shows the letters sit inside the run of words Santa Fe with

explanation.surface: Someone in the New Mexico city of Santa Fe is with one or two companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number, a couple or so, is a phrase meaning a handful.

clue.text: Return to the old island

indicators.note: Return tells us to read the pieces from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: An invitation to go back to the island of one's past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns the whole two-word run round, reading its letters from end to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in a river, especially the Thames, is called this in British English.

clue.text: Writer's swindles leading to Victor being put in cooler

indicators.note: leading puts the swindles first, ahead of what follows in the word

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, so swindles gives dos
taken as written

indicators.note: being put in places the letter for Victor inside the cool-box word

parts.note: an Esky is an Australian brand name for a portable cool box
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer's frauds end with a man called Victor locked in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' wants to be slang for jail; it is the Australian cool box ESKY, into which 'being put in' places V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist of Crime and Punishment is a famous author.

clue.text: One tripping from the States to Vatican is rather excited

indicators.note: rather excited suggests the words to Vatican is are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: An American tourist going to the Vatican is quite thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' means taking a trip, not stumbling; the word is American for holidaymaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An American holidaymaker takes trips, so is a traveller from the US.

clue.text: Such as the M1 will sever bloody arm

indicators.note: will sever means the roads piece cuts the other word in two

parts.note: bloody is a mild swear word starting with B, so it is a B-word
the M1, the motorway from London to Leeds, is one of the roads

explanation.surface: A motorway like the M1 will slice through a bloody limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb. 'Bloody' is itself a swear word beginning with B, which 'will sever' cuts open.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a broad-bladed sword is one such weapon.

clue.text: Violent film? Film me!

parts.note: film means shoot, and in a down entry the letters EM read upwards spell me

explanation.surface: A request to be filmed, or a gory movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: SHOOT (film) then EM UP, since EM written upward in a down grid is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun-heavy action movie or video game full of mayhem is this genre.

clue.text: Unable to speak a common language

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot talk a shared tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Can't means not able; cant also means to use the jargon or slang of a particular group.

clue.text: Stone's appeal to China?

parts.note: O is the exclamation used when calling out to someone, as in O Lord
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A gem that might appeal to buyers in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a PAL. 'O pal!' is a call to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone is a precious stone with a milky play of colour.

clue.text: Durable toy suffering damage? Hardly!

indicators.note: suffering damage tells us the words durable toy are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Does a sturdy plaything suffer damage? Hardly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' looks like 'scarcely' but means in a hard, stubborn way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting stubbornly and unyieldingly is behaving in a hard-hearted manner.

clue.text: Film reveals bum dealings

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare backside, so reveals bum gives moons
truck means dealings, as in having no truck with someone

explanation.surface: A movie exposes some shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is British slang for backside, not 'bad'; to moon is to show it. TRUCK is dealings, as in 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1987 romantic comedy starring Cher is a well-known movie.

clue.text: Jack Ketch's head and body

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of Ketch's

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Jack Ketch, the notorious hangman, deals with head and body.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner; here 'Jack' is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in a pack of cards is also called by this older name.

clue.text: I'm sworn in also at home

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie within the run of words also at home

explanation.surface: Someone sworn in at home as well as elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sworn in' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is the hiding signal and the definition is 'I'm sworn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise is something sworn, so it can say of itself that it is sworn.

clue.text: Pricy letter-opener

explanation.surface: An expensive gadget for slitting envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly goods are expensive; the greeting word also starts most correspondence, as in a salutation to Sir.

clue.text: Take Ten, noted sand-dancer

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
ten is written with the figures 1 and 0, read as IO

explanation.surface: A famous beach dancer takes a ten-minute break.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duran Duran song says 'her name is ___ and she dances on the sand'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title girl of a 1982 pop hit dances on the sand, so she is a famous beach dancer.

clue.text: Greek courses contain hidden feature, moving around theatrical circles

indicators.note: contain means the Greek dishes hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: mezzes are small Greek and Middle Eastern starter dishes

indicators.note: moving around means the word for the hidden feature is turned back to front

parts.note: a Nina is a hidden message or theme concealed in a crossword grid

explanation.surface: Greek starters hide something as people circulate round the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving around' turns the hidden-feature word back to front before the Greek dishes hold it. A Nina is crossword slang for a message concealed in a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the lowest balconies in a theatre, curved tiers of seating above the stalls.

clue.text: Maximally detailed President's present influence

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the last letter cut off

parts.note: at most means to the greatest extent, maximally
P is a standard abbreviation for President
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A president's gift, described in full detail, exerts influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means de-tailed: AT MOST loses its last letter to give ATMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pervading mood or tone of a place is an aura that affects those in it.

clue.text: Intimate Scot's twaddle, addressing mum's chum

parts.note: a letter addressed to someone is marked to them
sh goes with mum as a call for silence, as in mum's the word

explanation.surface: A Scot's familiar talk is nonsense when aimed at mother's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots the word means neat, comfortable or friendly; elsewhere it is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or rubbish is the everyday British sense; in Scots dialect it means snug and familiar.
